title: Teach a robot something new.
name: LeRobot
summary: A shared toolkit for robot learning, with datasets, trained models, and examples to help you get started.
why: A practical entry point into robotics research. Start with the documentation and a supported simulation or dataset before choosing hardware.

title: Make your creative process visible.
name: ComfyUI
summary: Build image and media workflows by connecting visual nodes. Experiment, compare, and keep the process reproducible.
why: A visual workflow lets you trace how an image was made and change one step at a time. Check model licenses before commercial use.

title: Play with a new kind of instrument.
name: Magenta RealTime
summary: Explore real-time music generation as an instrument for improvisation and creative collaboration.
why: The interesting question is what you can perform with it. Follow the setup guide and experiment with short musical ideas.

title: Ask a better next question.
name: Khanmigo
summary: Explore Khan Academy's AI tools for learning and teaching, built around guided questions and classroom support.
why: A useful place to explore guided learning. Availability, access, and pricing vary, so review the current details on Khan Academy's website.

title: Explore the shapes of life.
name: AlphaFold Protein Structure Database
summary: Search predicted protein structures and inspect the confidence information behind each prediction.
why: A way to see AI-assisted scientific work first-hand. Predictions include uncertainty and are not substitutes for experimental validation.

title: Build a world an agent can learn.
name: Unity ML-Agents
summary: Use game environments to train and study intelligent agents, with examples and a documented learning toolkit.
why: Games make learning behavior visible. Try an included example before designing a new training environment.

title: Inspect the reasoning behind the numbers.
name: FinRobot
summary: An open framework for experimenting with AI agents in financial analysis and research.
why: Use sample data to understand the workflow and validate outputs against original filings. This is a research resource, not investment advice.

title: Give a local model a home.
name: Ollama
summary: Run supported language models locally and connect them to your own experiments and applications.
why: A starting point for learning about local inference. Your hardware, model choice, and its license determine what you can run.
